title: EHR Alerts to Improve GLP-1 Medication and Continuous Glucose Monitor Prescribing in Primary Care
official: Evaluation of Quality Improvement Initiative to Improve GLP-1 and CGM Prescription Rates
summary: This randomized quality improvement study will evaluate whether pop-up alerts in the electronic health record (EHR) increase prescribing of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) medications and continuous glucose monitors (CGMs) for eligible patients with diabetes. The study will be conducted at nine Montefiore Medical Group primary care sites. Primary care providers will be randomly assigned to either receive the alerts or not receive them. The alerts will remind providers that a patient is eligible for a GLP-1 RA, a CGM, or both, and will help them choose the option covered by the patient's insurance. Providers in both groups will use their own clinical judgment in deciding whether to prescribe. The study will use information already recorded in patients' medical records.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Meet Klompas definition of diabetes
* Has at least one primary care visit, in-person or telehealth, during the study period
* Is covered by Medicare or Medicaid

Additional inclusion criteria for the GLP-1 portion of the OPA alert:

* GLP-1 component: HbA1c ≥ 9 on most recent lab test in the past 12 months and a BMI ≥ 25) OR BMI ≥ 30, and no GLP-1 prescription in the past 12 months

Additional inclusion criteria for the CGM portion of the OPA alert:

* CGM component: Insulin prescription in the past 12 months and no CGM prescription in the past 12 months

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients seen by residents during their first visit
